stem: Ira cuts a paper rectangle into pieces $P$ and $Q$ and rearranges them into a new outline with no gaps and no overlaps. The diagram shows the original rectangle and the rearranged outline.

options.text: The new outline must have smaller area because its outer path looks different.
Equal area is what forces the rearranged outline to be a rectangle again.
The rearranged outline has the same area as the original rectangle.
Area stays equal even if she throws piece $Q$ away before rearranging.

teacher.key_rationale: Cutting and rearranging with no gaps or overlaps preserves area. A different outline does not change that. Saying equal area forces a rectangle reverses the relation. Dropping a piece leaves the equal-area condition.
